instrument_name: Conn. Gen. Stat. 31-58(i) Minimum fair wage (chapter 558)
figure_or_rule_carried: Statutory floor 15.00 USD/h from 2023-06-01; indexed every 1 January by the % change in the ECI (wages and salaries, all civilian workers) over the 12 months ending 30 June of the preceding year, rounded to the nearest cent; Labor Commissioner announces by 15 October; never less than federal minimum + 0.5%; minors under 18 (non-emancipated): not less than 85% of minimum for first 90 days or 10.10 USD, whichever greater
verification_method: inspected directly (Wayback 20261024200754 copy of official chapter; cga.ct.gov curl 000)

instrument_name: Conn. Gen. Stat. 31-60(b)-(d) tip credit and board allowances
figure_or_rule_carried: Tipped hotel/restaurant employees (non-bartenders): employer share 6.38 USD/h; bartenders: 8.23 USD/h (tip credit = minimum fair wage minus employer share); other industries tip credit not over 0.35 USD/h; meal allowances 0.85 USD full meal / 0.45 USD light meal

instrument_name: Conn. Gen. Stat. 31-76b to 31-76c overtime
figure_or_rule_carried: Overtime 1.5x regular rate over 40 hours in a workweek (no daily overtime in 31-76c); regular rate includes all remuneration except gifts, non-work-period pay, discretionary bonuses, bona fide plan contributions, premium pay listed in 31-76b(1)(E)-(F)

instrument_name: Conn. Gen. Stat. 31-71b, 31-71i, 31-71k pay frequency, pay day and method
figure_or_rule_carried: Pay weekly or once every two weeks on a regular pay day designated in advance; pay period end not more than 8 days before pay day; pay day on a non-work day -> preceding work day; methods: cash, negotiable check, direct deposit on employee's written or electronic request, payroll card (employee must have the option of direct deposit and check, and authorize the card voluntarily in writing or electronically); Commissioner may waive to less frequent but at least monthly

instrument_name: Conn. Gen. Stat. 31-71c and 31-76k final pay and accrued fringe benefits
figure_or_rule_carried: Voluntary quit: full wages by the next regular pay day; discharge: by the business day next succeeding discharge; layoff/labour dispute suspension: next regular pay day. Accrued vacation/holidays/sick days paid on termination only if employer policy or CBA provides it, at not less than the earned average rate for the accrual period

instrument_name: Conn. Gen. Stat. 31-71e withholding of part of wages
figure_or_rule_carried: Deductions only if (1) required/empowered by state or federal law, (2) written authorization on a form approved by the Labor Commissioner, (3) written authorization for medical/surgical/hospital care without benefit to employer, (4) automatic-enrollment 401(k)/403(b)/408/408A/457 or CT Retirement Security Program, (5) another state's income-tax withholding required for services there or residents there

instrument_name: Conn. Gen. Stat. 31-71f hiring notice
figure_or_rule_carried: Written notice at hire of rate of remuneration, hours, wage payment schedule; policies on wages, vacation pay, sick leave available in writing or posted; domestic workers: extended written notice (duties, leave accrual, board/lodging charges, complaint route)

authority: Office of the Governor of Connecticut (announcing the Labor Commissioner's adjustment)

instrument_name: Governor's press release: minimum wage 17.48 USD from 2027-01-01 (ECI +3.2%)
authority: Office of the Governor of Connecticut (announcing the Labor Commissioner's adjustment)
figure_or_rule_carried: Minimum wage 17.48 USD/h from 2027-01-01 (from 16.94); ECI +3.2% for 12 months to 2026-06-30. Derivation: 16.94 x 1.032 = 17.48208 -> 17.48. Tipped employer share stays 6.38 / 8.23 (fixed in 31-60(d)(3)); minors 85% first 90 days = 14.86 (2027), 14.40 (2026)

instrument_name: IP 2026(1) Circular CT: CT-W4 codes and default withholding
figure_or_rule_carried: Form CT-W4 (Rev. 12/25) codes A/B/C/D/E/F by filing status and income; no CT-W4 -> withhold flat 6.99% without exemption; Code E (exempt) certificates expire 15 February, new CT-W4 required or withhold 6.99% from 16 February; send copies of CT-W4 claiming exempt to DRS where expected annual wages exceed 36,000 (MFS) / 45,000 (single) / 57,000 (HoH) / 72,000 (MFJ) = 3x max personal exemption; MSRRA claim needs LES + dependent ID; CT wages follow federal withholding wage definition (fringe benefits, supplemental, sick pay, severance)
verification_method: inspected directly (pdftotext of held PDF md5 a64b2bbb855163fb832396939efc74ef)

instrument_name: IP 2026(1) Circular CT: supplemental compensation
figure_or_rule_carried: No flat supplemental rate. Paid with regular wages: tax on the total as a single payment. Paid separately: if no withholding on regular wages, add regular + supplemental and compute; if withheld, compute on combined regular + supplemental for the last regular period and withhold the difference (aggregate method only)

instrument_name: IP 2026(1) Circular CT: remitter classes, CT-941, CT-W3, W-2 filing, EFT
figure_or_rule_carried: All withholding forms filed and paid electronically (myconneCT / EFT; waiver DRS-EWVR). Remitter class by 12-month lookback (ended 2025-06-30 for 2026): weekly > 10,000 (Wednesday after the Sat-Fri weekly period); monthly > 2,000 to 10,000 (15th of next month); quarterly <= 2,000 (last day of month after quarter); most new employers quarterly. CT-941 quarterly due Apr 30/Jul 31/Oct 31/Jan 31 even with no tax (+10 days if fully paid); CT-941 required even for federal 944 filers; annual filer status by request by 31 March. CT-W3 + all W-2s by 31 January via myconneCT, options: key-and-send, EFW2 upload, pre-defined CSV; W-2 box 15 'CT' + CT Tax Registration Number, box 16 residents all wages / nonresidents CT-service wages; 5 USD per information return penalty max 2,000/yr; e-file waiver CT-8508 30 days before due

instrument_name: IP 2026(1) Circular CT: household, agricultural, seasonal employers; military
figure_or_rule_carried: Household employer: CT withholding not required, voluntary by agreement; if registered, one CT-941 HHE for the year due 15 April; CT-W3 HHE + state W-2 due 31 January whether or not registered. Agricultural: must withhold CT where federal withholding is required on cash wages (Pub. 51); annual filer status (one CT-941 due 31 January) if 943 filer. Seasonal: CT-941 only for active quarters on request. Military pay to nonresident servicemembers not CT wages; CT-resident military pay subject regardless of station; MSRRA spouses exempt on CT-W4 with LES

instrument_name: IP 2026(1) Circular CT: new hire reporting to CT DOL
authority: Connecticut Department of Revenue Services (stating CT DOL duty)
article_or_section: Form CT-W4 page 2 'Report New and Rehired Employees to the Department of Labor'
figure_or_rule_carried: Employers with offices in CT or transacting business in CT report new hires and rehires (separated > 60 consecutive days) to CT DOL within 20 days of hire; channels: CT New Hire Reporting website www1.ctdol.state.ct.us/newhires, fax CT-W4 to 800-816-1108, or mail CT-W4 to CT DOL Office of Research; CT-W4 itself carries the new/rehired flag, hire date and FEIN

instrument_name: Conn. Gen. Stat. 31-222(b) UI taxable wages (indexed wage base; other-state wage credit)
figure_or_rule_carried: Taxable wage base 25,000 for 2024; from 2025 prior-year base adjusted by % change in ECI (wages and salaries, all civilian workers, 12 months to 30 June preceding) rounded to nearest 100 USD. Derivation: 26,100 x 1.036 = 27,039.6 -> 27,000 (2026, matches US-CTP9V-001); 25,000 x 1.042 = 26,050 -> 26,100 (2025; ECI 4.2% implied by min wage 15.69 -> 16.35, not separately sourced). Remuneration on which contributions were paid to another state's UI law for employment there counts toward the CT maximum (wage-base credit: yes). Employer FICA paid without deduction for domestic/agricultural employees excluded

instrument_name: Conn. Gen. Stat. 31-222(a) UI employment definition and exclusions
figure_or_rule_carried: Domestic service covered if cash wages >= 1,000 USD in any calendar quarter (current or preceding year); agricultural labor covered if >= 20,000 USD cash in a quarter or 10+ workers on 20 days in 20 weeks; churches/religious orders and ordained ministers excluded; excluded: family employment (spouse, child under 18 employed by parent), students at own school and spouse in student-aid work, student nurses/interns, newspaper carriers under 18, co-op students in credit programs, service covered by another state's UI law, US/other-state government service; non-profit 501(a) service under 50 USD/quarter

instrument_name: Conn. Gen. Stat. 31-225a(j) quarterly UI wage report and electronic filing
figure_or_rule_carried: Quarterly listing of each employee's name, SSN and wages paid in the quarter; electronic filing and electronic payment mandatory for employers and agents unless written waiver requested 30 days before due (undue hardship); late fee 25 USD, wrong registration number fee 25 USD. NEW: from Q3 2026 employers MAY add occupation, hours worked and ZIP code of primary worksite per employee (optional)

instrument_name: Conn. Gen. Stat. 31-254(b) state directory of new hires
figure_or_rule_carried: Within 20 days of employment each employer with an office or transacting business in CT reports name, address and SSN of each new employee employed in CT to the Labor Department, by copy of the CT withholding certificate (CT-W4) or other means under regulation; electronic reporters per regulation

instrument_name: Conn. Gen. Stat. 31-49e, 31-49g, 31-49o, 31-49q Paid Family and Medical Leave (CT Paid Leave)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employee contribution set by the Authority, capped at 0.5% of subject earnings (31-222(b) total wages up to the Social Security contribution and benefit base, 42 USC 430); employer deducts each payroll period; no employer share. Employee = service to an employer in this state; employer = 1+ employees; excludes federal/state/municipal/boards of education/nonpublic schools except opted-in covered public employees. Covered employee: >= 2,325 USD subject earnings in highest base-period quarter. Benefit 95% of base weekly earnings up to 40x minimum wage + 60% above, max 60x minimum wage (2026: 1,016.40 USD/week = 60 x 16.94; 2027: 1,048.80 = 60 x 17.48, derived); employee may elect income-tax withholding on benefits. Private plan: no fund contribution; employer may withhold up to the fund rate. Written notice at hire and annually (31-49q)
verification_method: inspected directly (statute text read; benefit max derived arithmetically)

instrument_name: Conn. Gen. Stat. 31-57r to 31-57s paid sick leave (as amended by P.A. 23-101 and P.A. 24-8)
figure_or_rule_carried: Phase-in by headcount in CT (payroll for the week containing 1 January): 25+ from 2025-01-01; 11+ from 2026-01-01; 1+ from 2027-01-01. Accrual 1 hour per 30 hours worked, 1-hour increments, max 40 hours/year; carry-over up to 40 hours (use cap 40/yr) or front-load; use from day 120 of employment; pay at the greater of normal hourly wage (variable-rate: average hourly wage of prior pay period) or minimum wage; FLSA-exempt presumed 40 h/week; other PTO counts if same uses and accrual rate; no payout of unused leave on termination unless policy/CBA provides; excludes seasonal employees (<=120 days/yr) and construction multiemployer-plan members

instrument_name: CT Paid Leave Authority: contributions and remittance pages (2026)
article_or_section: Contributions; Remit Contributions; Batch Process; I am an Employer
figure_or_rule_carried: Board kept the 2026 contribution rate at 0.5% (employee-paid, employer deducts and remits). Base: total wages incl. vacation/holiday pay, tips, commissions, severance, cash value of in-kind; exclude benefits excluded from FICA wages; cap = Social Security contribution and benefit base, per employer (multiple employers each withhold to the cap; employee claims refund). Remit quarterly: due last day of the quarter, no penalty/interest if paid by the last day of the month after quarter-end; late: penalty + 1%/month non-compounding interest. Channels: My Account portal (File + Pay) or batch SFTP return files in XML or CSV per the CT Paid Leave File Specification Toolkit (PDF), NACHA ACH credit; separate SFTP from other CT taxes. Notice of Employee Rights at hire and annually; Employment Verification form must be returned by the claim deadline

instrument_name: Conn. Gen. Stat. 31-53(f)-(h) prevailing wage certified payroll and thresholds
figure_or_rule_carried: Employers on covered public works keep wage/hour/classification records and file weekly certified payrolls with the contracting public agency (public record; failure to file = class D felony, fine up to 5,000 USD). Not applicable where new construction total cost < 1,000,000 USD or remodeling/repair/alteration total < 100,000 USD

instrument_name: Conn. Gen. Stat. 52-361a wage execution (creditor garnishment)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer delivers copy to debtor; execution stayed 20 days after service then continuing levy. Maximum weekly levy = lesser of 25% of disposable earnings or disposable earnings exceeding 40 x the higher of the federal minimum wage or the CT minimum fair wage (2026: 40 x 16.94 = 677.60 USD/week protected; 2027: 699.20; derived) - stricter than CCPA's 30 x federal minimum. Only one execution satisfied at a time; support withholding under 52-362 has priority
verification_method: inspected directly (statute text read; protected amount derived arithmetically)

instrument_name: Conn. Gen. Stat. 52-362 income withholding for support
figure_or_rule_carried: Withholding only against income exceeding the greater of 85% of the first 145 USD/week of disposable income or the 15 USC 1673 exemption; start no later than the first pay period after 14 days from service; remit to the State Disbursement Unit within 7 business days of pay date; multiple orders allocated pro rata by the SDU with priority to current support; support withholding has priority over 52-361a wage executions; DSS standard employer notice and claim form

instrument_name: Conn. Gen. Stat. 42-470 and 42-471 Social Security numbers and personal information
figure_or_rule_carried: No public posting/display of SSN, no SSN on access cards, no SSN over the internet unless secure/encrypted, no SSN-only web login; use required by law or for internal verification/administration allowed. Anyone holding personal information must safeguard and destroy before disposal; anyone collecting SSNs must publish a privacy protection policy. No statute requiring SSN truncation on pay statements located (31-13a does not require SSN on the record)

instrument_name: Conn. Gen. Stat. 31-13a(b) and 31-66 electronic statements and record retention
figure_or_rule_carried: Pay record with each wage payment (hours, gross with straight time and overtime separate - not required for employees exempt from time records/overtime - itemised deductions, net); electronic only with explicit employee consent and a secure, private means to access and print, with confidentiality safeguards. Hours and wages records kept at the place of employment for 3 years

instrument_name: Public Act 26-12 (Sub. HB 5003) omnibus workforce act - payroll-relevant sections
figure_or_rule_carried: In force. Sec. 38 eff. 2026-10-01: employers with 100+ employees (incl. state and political subdivisions) must create a pay-code guide (overtime and most common pay differentials, >= 10 codes if applicable) posted on the website in English, Spanish and other most common employee languages, with a dispute contact; give the URL at hire and PRINT THE URL ON EACH PAY RECORD (31-13a(a)) - a third-party payroll company's compliant guide satisfies it. Sec. 40 eff. 2026-10-01: minor-league baseball players under CBA excluded from 'employee' for minimum wage/overtime. Sec. 6: no tip credit toward minimum wage for cannabis establishment employees (per OLR summary; section text not parsed). Sec. 56 eff. 2027-01-01: 31-72 double damages for unpaid wages/31-76k fringe benefits, good-faith defence limits to single; subcontractor wage claims against general contractor for contracts from 2027-01-01. Level: employer pay statement and wage payment. NOTE: the held ch. 557 Wayback copy (2026-10-20) still shows 31-13a without subsection (c) - codification lag

instrument_name: CT DOL Employer's Guide to Unemployment Compensation (updated 2026-04-23) - local copy
article_or_section: pp. 17, 20-21 (Taxable wage base; Filing of UI Tax and Wage Reports; due dates; penalties); Separation Packet UC-21/UC-21A
figure_or_rule_carried: Local copy (md5 5707bd7eb7bea69f7e580194c5b1e161) replacing the MANUAL row. Quarterly Tax and Wage Report filed and paid electronically via ReEmployCT (manual entry, file upload, TPA, or FSET); zero-wage report required; corporate bulk upload for subsidiaries requires TPA registration; due 4/30, 7/31, 10/31, 1/31 (reimbursing employers +15 days); next business day rule; amendments within 3 years; late payment interest + penalty greater of 50 USD or 10% if unpaid 30 days; late file fee 25 USD. instrument_name: CT DOL ReEmployCT Tax and Wage Report upload file format (276-character fixed length)
article_or_section: S record and T record layouts (4 pp.)

instrument_name: Conn. Gen. Stat. 31-51kk and 31-51ll CT Family and Medical Leave (job-protected)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer = 1+ employees (excludes municipalities, boards of education, nonpublic schools); 12 workweeks per 12-month period (+2 for incapacitation during pregnancy per 31-51ll); where employer pays fewer than 12 weeks, the rest may be unpaid or compensated through CT Paid Leave (31-49g) - payroll interaction: CTPL benefits are paid by the Authority, not through payroll; employee may elect income-tax withholding on benefits

instrument_name: Conn. Gen. Stat. 31-58(e) minimum wage coverage exclusions (as amended by PA 26-12 sec. 40)
figure_or_rule_carried: 'Employee' for minimum wage/overtime excludes: seasonal camps/resorts open <= 6 months; domestic service in a private home EXCEPT FLSA-defined domestic service employment (so FLSA-covered domestic workers are covered); bona fide executive/administrative/professional (Labor Commissioner regs); federal employees; volunteers of nonprofit/charitable/religious organisations where no employment relationship; college head residents/RAs; babysitting; FLSA outside salesmen; nonprofit theatre (<= 7 months/yr); state military duty; from 2026-10-01 minor-league baseball players under CBA
